data.name: CableHelpTitle
data.value: A plugged-in device Windows cannot read

data.name: CableHelpIntro
data.value: The phone may well be charging, which only proves power. The data wires carry nothing usable. Here are the leads, from the most common to the rarest.

data.name: CableHelpSteps
data.value:
Try another cable. Many cables shipped with a charger have no data wires, and a damaged data cable gives exactly this fault.
Try a USB 2.0 port, at the back of the machine rather than the front: enumeration is more forgiving there and the path is shorter.
Restart, do not shut down. With Windows fast startup, shutting down and powering back on does not reinitialise the USB controllers; only "Restart" does.
Clean the phone's connector. Pocket dust keeps the data pins from making contact while charging still works.
Cross the tests: another device on this port, and this phone on another PC. You will then know which of the three is at fault.

data.name: AdbShellUserAccessDenied
data.value: The phone refused the PC access to that profile. If it is a secure folder, unlock it on the phone before launching. Otherwise turn on “USB debugging (security settings)” in the developer options.

data.name: ScrcpyDisplayTimeoutWithAudio
data.value: The phone did not open a virtual display in time. Try without sound first: on some tablets, turning it on is enough to stop the display from opening.

data.name: BrandSamsungWarning
data.value: If the tablet is not detected at all, turn off “Auto blocker” in Settings > Security and privacy, then “Block USB connections” in the other security settings. A secure folder has to be unlocked before launching, or the game will not be found in it.

data.name: BrandOnePlusWarning
data.value: Also turn on “USB debugging (security settings)” and “Install via USB” in the same menu. Without the first one the picture shows but the mouse and keyboard do nothing.

data.name: BrandVivoWarning
data.value: Also turn on “USB debugging (security settings)” and “Install via USB” in the same menu. Without the first one the picture shows but the mouse and keyboard do nothing.

data.name: DeadInputHelp
data.value: The mouse does nothing in the window?

data.name: DeadInputExplanation
data.value: The picture shows, the window opens, and yet clicks and keystrokes do nothing. No error appears, because there is none: the device agrees to show its screen, but not to receive your gestures. That is a separate permission, and it is granted on the phone.

data.name: DeadInputTestHelp
data.value: The check asks the device to accept an input event, using the key Android calls “unknown”, which triggers nothing anywhere. It says in one second what otherwise takes an evening to find out.

data.name: DeadInputTestWorks
data.value: The device accepts input simulation. If clicks still do nothing, the cause is below, not here.

data.name: DeadInputTestDenied

data.name: DeadInputTestUnknown
data.value: No verdict. The device answered something unexpected, and guessing would be worse than saying nothing.

data.name: DeadInputTestNoDevice
data.value: No device connected. Plug one in or pair it, then run the check again.

data.name: DeadInputSecurityHelp
data.value: In the developer options, turn on the line whose description reads “Grant permissions and simulate input via USB debugging”. Depending on the brand it is called “USB debugging (security settings)”. This is by far the most common cause.

data.name: DeadInputCable
data.value: The cable has to carry data

data.name: DeadInputCableHelp
data.value: When the phone asks for the connection mode, pick “File transfer”, not “Charging”. A cable left on charging lets the screen show while refusing everything else. If the question never appears, try another cable: many cables shipped with a charger have no data wires.

data.name: SimulatedKeyboardTip
data.value: Present the keyboard to the phone as a plugged-in keyboard, instead of typing through its on-screen one.

data.name: SimulatedKeyboardHelp
data.value: Turn this on when the window answers the mouse but nothing you type appears: the on-screen keyboard of some brands swallows the characters. In exchange, the phone reads your keys through its own Android layout, so set that layout to match your PC keyboard, or an AZERTY will type as QWERTY.

data.name: DeadInputRevokeHelp
data.value: In the developer options, press “Revoke USB debugging authorisations”, unplug the device, plug it back in, and accept the prompt again. It clears an authorisation left half granted, and it is the step that unblocks the cases where everything looks correctly set.

data.name: DeadInputToggleDeveloper
data.value: Turn it all off, restart, turn it all back on

data.name: DeadInputToggleDeveloperHelp
data.value: Unplug the phone from the PC first. Then turn off the debugging switches, up to three depending on the brand: USB debugging, install via USB, and USB debugging (security settings). Restart the phone, turn them back on once it has restarted, then plug it back in on “File transfer” and accept the prompt. The order matters, and so does the restart: turning them back on without it often leaves the setting ticked without being applied.

data.name: BrandStandardName
data.value: Stock Android: Pixel, Motorola, ASUS, TCL, other

data.name: BrandStandardCloneNote
data.value: Stock Android has no cloning feature. The way round it is to add a second user, then install the game there from the Play Store. DT Hub opens each profile on its own display, with no switching back and forth.

data.name: BrandStandardBuildNumberPath
data.value: Settings › About phone, or About tablet

data.name: BrandXiaomiCloneNote
data.value: This brand also offers Second space, which creates a whole separate space rather than a simple copy. Either will do: DT Hub sees the instances both ways.

data.name: BrandXiaomiBatteryPath
data.value: Settings › Apps › Manage apps › DOFUS Touch › Battery saver

data.name: BrandXiaomiBatteryNote
data.value: This brand is the most aggressive of the lot. Lock the game in the recents view as well, by pulling its card down: without that lock, HyperOS closes it after a few minutes whatever the battery setting says.

data.name: BrandXiaomiBuildNumberPath
data.value: Settings › About phone, or About tablet

data.name: BrandXiaomiBuildNumberLabel
data.value: HyperOS version, or MIUI version on older models

data.name: BrandXiaomiWarning
data.value: Turn on USB debugging (security settings): without it the picture shows but the mouse and keyboard do nothing. USB debugging sometimes also asks for a SIM card and a signed-in Xiaomi account. If clicks stay dead, turn off Stylus handwriting, right at the bottom of the developer options.

data.name: BrandSamsungClonePath
data.value: Settings › Security and privacy › Secure Folder

data.name: BrandSamsungCloneNote
data.value: Dual Messenger only duplicates messaging apps, so it will not do for a game. Secure Folder takes any app, and asks for a Samsung account. It has to be unlocked before launching: locked, the game inside it stays out of reach from the PC.

data.name: BrandSamsungBatteryPath
data.value: Settings › Battery › Background usage limits › Never sleeping apps

data.name: BrandSamsungBatteryNote
data.value: Turn off Auto optimise daily as well, under Settings > Device care: switched back on, it puts the game back to sleep after a few days.

data.name: BrandSamsungBuildNumberPath
data.value: Settings › About phone, or About tablet › Software information

data.name: BrandOnePlusBatteryFeature
data.value: Allow background activity, set to Unrestricted

data.name: BrandOnePlusBatteryPath
data.value: Settings › Battery › Battery usage › DOFUS Touch

data.name: BrandOnePlusBatteryNote
data.value: On these skins, a separate auto-clean can close apps when the screen goes off. It is turned off under Settings > Battery > More settings.

data.name: BrandOnePlusBuildNumberLabel
data.value: Build number, or Version number depending on the release installed

data.name: BrandHonorCloneNote
data.value: On builds without Google services, installing the second copy may mean going through the maker's own store.

data.name: BrandHonorBatteryPath
data.value: Settings › Battery › App launch › DOFUS Touch

data.name: BrandHonorBatteryNote
data.value: Switch the game to manual management, then turn on the three switches offered, Run in background included. Automatic management closes the game whatever you set elsewhere.

data.name: BrandHonorBuildNumberPath
data.value: Settings › About phone, or About tablet

data.name: BrandHonorWarning
data.value: On builds without Google services, wireless debugging is sometimes missing. The USB cable is then the only way.

data.name: BrandVivoCloneNote
data.value: Depending on the Funtouch or OriginOS release, the feature sits under Apps, or under Apps and permissions.

data.name: BrandVivoBatteryFeature
data.value: Background power consumption, set to Allow

data.name: BrandVivoBatteryPath
data.value: Settings › Battery › Background power consumption management › DOFUS Touch

data.name: BrandVivoBatteryNote
data.value: Turn on Autostart for the game as well. These skins are among the quickest to close an app the moment it leaves the foreground.

data.name: BrandVivoBuildNumberPath
data.value: Settings › About phone, or About tablet › Software version

data.name: BrandVivoBuildNumberLabel
data.value: Version number, or Build number depending on the release installed

data.name: BrandAmazonCloneNote
data.value: Fire OS has no cloning feature and its profiles are not Android's: DT Hub will most likely see only one instance there. For trials only.

data.name: BrandAmazonBatteryFeature
data.value: Battery optimisation, to be turned off

data.name: BrandAmazonWarning
data.value: Fire OS has no Play Store: DOFUS Touch is not distributed there, and installing it means going through an APK file. This card describes the steps; it does not promise the game will run.
